$comment: Gate registry for the gates that are NOT yet part of the root `check:all` contract.
`check:all` in <workspace>/package.json remains the single source of truth for the
contract tier, so those gates are deliberately NOT duplicated here — that would create
two authorities for the same fact.
workspace - run once; argv template may use {workspace}
repo      - run once per governed repository; argv template may use {repo}
contract  - must exit 0; a non-zero exit fails the matrix
guardrail - known debt; must not grow beyond `baseline`; a higher count fails the matrix
Lower it whenever debt is paid down; never raise it without an explicit decision.

Promoted on 2026-09-11 into root check:all (single authority for the contract tier): check:app-permission-tiers, check:app-runtime-hosting-debt, check:application-layering, check:bootstrap-access-token-lifecycle-standard, check:discovery-standard, check:iam-workspace-paths, check:external-submodule-rule, check:rust-manifest-standard

PNPM_SCRIPT_SPEC.md section on canonical root scripts. 677 script violations across 20 of 87 repositories on 2026-09-11, down from 798. 34 repositories wire this gate individually, but the workspace aggregate never ran it, so the others were unchecked. This is the root cause of the 'no aggregate' warnings in the locale gate wiring audit: a repository with no `verify` script has no aggregate to wire any gate into. Baseline measured with run-gate-matrix.mjs#countItems, not by hand; it fell 817 -> 798 when the documentation-examples scan stopped validating git-ignored `.workbuddy/` agent memory as shipped documentation, and 798 -> 677 via align-pnpm-lifecycle-facade.mjs on 2026-09-11, which took passed repositories from 62 to 67 and edited only each repository's own package.json. Two unenforced MUST clauses were closed here on 2026-09-11 with zero fleet impact, verified before implementing: (1) the public-verb/private-hook pairing of section 2 is now bidirectional for build/test/check/verify/clean. A public verb delegating to the facade without its `_sdkwork:<verb>` hook is a script that cannot run, because runPrivateLifecycleScript returns null for a missing hook and sdkwork-app then throws 'missing private lifecycle hook'; a `_sdkwork:<verb>` hook that no public verb selects is unreachable dead weight. (2) Section 2 requires an application invoking `pnpm exec sdkwork-app` to declare a pinned `@sdkwork/app-topology`. Both clauses were 100 percent satisfied by convention across the fleet (0 mismatches, 53/53 declare the dependency) but enforced by no gate, so the next repository could have regressed either silently. The rules also guard the migration: they refuse a half-done conversion that adds `pnpm exec sdkwork-app <verb>` without moving the real command into the matching hook. Residual debt is concentrated: sdkwork-birdcoder2 contributes 571 namespace findings from the upstream dsh script surface, and 15 repositories still lack `build` because no faithful command can be derived - those ship browser or Flutter clients whose build is per-architecture and per-environment (build:pc:*, build:h5:*), so `cargo build` or a single guessed command would be a plausible but wrong answer, and the gap is reported as an owner decision rather than filled with a placeholder. Round 8 (2026-09-12) took the baseline 677 -> 617 and passed repositories 67 -> 84: the checker now completes the section 4 allowed first-segment list (up/down/import were allowed by the checker but missing from the standard, and schema-registry was missing from both), and a drift-guard test asserts the two lists stay identical, so the class of defect where a name is authorized by only one of them can no longer recur. align-pnpm-lifecycle-facade.mjs gained two derivations that are independent of the lifecycle facade: section 7 api:assembly:materialize|validate for every application root owning crates/sdkwork-api-<code>-assembly (added to drama, generations, mall, video), and the section 2 default dev runtime normalization that re-homes the existing command under pnpm dev:<target>:postgres:standalone without rewriting it. sdkwork-order iprune:openapi was deleted rather than renamed: its ORDER_OWNED_TAG_PREFIXES no longer match the order-prefixed tags in the authority, so running it would have filtered every tag out and written the file back. tools/align-pnpm-stop-scripts.mjs was retired: it had zero references and its only job was to inject the workspace-wide process killer into any repository missing a stop, which is exactly the scoped-stop violation now enforced. A missing or unscoped stop deliberately does NOT make a repository a facade-conversion target any more; handing stop to a facade that never started the session would replace working lifecycle scripts to fix a command that still could not find its processes, so that case is reported as an owner decision. The three remaining failures are all owner decisions: sdkwork-api-cloud-gateway keeps a bespoke development runner, sdkwork-superpowers is mis-declared as an application while shipping no runnable surface, and sdkwork-birdcoder2 carries the upstream deepseek-harness script surface.

MODULE_BIN_SPEC.md section 2.1, the placement contract. 138 violations across 100 governed repositories and 2689 audited script files on 2026-09-11, 74/100 modules aligned. This gate is the standard's declared 'single enforcement surface', but it was declared in sdkwork-specs/package.json only and was therefore in neither tier: no root `check:all` entry and no gate here, so the fleet could regress with nothing noticing. Promoted here to make it measurable. The count fell 157 -> 138 through two audited-class corrections, both of which were gate defects rather than repository debt. First, MODULE_BIN_SPEC section 2.2 makes the `.cmd` companion part of a platform family, yet SCRIPT_SUFFIXES stopped at `.ps1`, so every authored `.cmd`/`.bat` outside bin/ was invisible; widening the class added 15 findings while simultaneously making the gate honest. Second, the ignore probe called `git check-ignore` without `--no-index`, and `git check-ignore` consults the index before the exclude rules, so any scratch script that a bulk `git add` had committed was reported as SCRATCH-NOT-IGNORED even when `.gitignore` already matched it; adding `--no-index` removed that whole class (now 0 findings) and confirmed the surviving findings are genuine placement debt. Largest owners: sdkwork-superpowers 33, sdkwork-tts 17, sdkwork-agentstudio 9, sdkwork-birdcoder2 8, sdkwork-specs 7, sdkwork-terminal 7.

MODULE_BIN_SPEC.md sections 2 and 2.2, the bin/ entrypoint family and naming convention. 79 product modules audited, 79 pass, 0 violations on 2026-09-11. Unwired until now for the same reason as check:script-placement: declared in sdkwork-specs/package.json, present in neither tier. The tool also emits a `violations : N` line as of 2026-09-11, because run-gate-matrix.mjs#countItems reads that label and would otherwise record 0 for every run, which would make the gate decorative. Separately: 49 section 2.2 naming warnings remain in sdkwork-im (host-native surface awaiting a family token); warnings are visible debt by design and are not counted in this baseline.

REPOSITORY_BASELINE_SPEC.md section 2: a root .gitignore must not ignore directories the standards designate as authored content. The rule protects `bin/` (MODULE_BIN_SPEC.md section 2 makes it the module's only authored-script channel and defines no ignore provision) and `sdks/**/generated/` (SDK_WORKSPACE_GENERATION_SPEC.md regulates committed generated output). Measured 2026-09-11 before the aligner ran: 77 of 100 governed repositories ignored canonical content (75 the root `bin/` directory as `/bin/` or `/bin/*`, 9 `sdks/**/generated/`). 73 of those repositories shipped the nine canonical bin/ entrypoint scripts on disk and 69 of them were entirely untracked -- the standard's mandated entrypoints could not be committed while every other gate stayed green, because no gate reads the ignore file and `git status` looks clean. The `align:gitignore-standard` fixer removed 84 over-reaching entries from 77 files; the fleet is now 100/100 and the baseline is therefore 0.

APP_PC_ARCHITECTURE_SPEC.md section 11 and APP_H5_ARCHITECTURE_SPEC.md section 8 own the native host package rules; this gate is their executable form. It proves every native host package under a client root is architecture-explicit, is owned by the matching client root, keeps exactly one package per architecture, and carries its own ecosystem manifest - package.json for a PC, H5 or mini program root, and oh-package.json5, pubspec.yaml, build.gradle.kts or Package.swift for a Harmony, Flutter, native Android or native iOS root (HARMONY_APP_MOBILE_ARCHITECTURE_SPEC.md section 4) - rather than a package.json that ohpm, Gradle, pub and SwiftPM never read. An earlier revision demanded package.json of every root and reported five false findings against the Harmony roots of sdkwork-agents, sdkwork-appstore, sdkwork-cloudrouter, sdkwork-knowledgebase and sdkwork-webserver. The retired -pc-desktop alias for the Tauri host, and an inert package.json inside a native host package, are reported as migration debt and fail only under --strict. MEASURED 2026-09-17: 6 items, and all six are real host-name defects - sdkwork-appstore-pc-host and sdkwork-appstore-h5-host are generic architecture-free names, and sdkwork-autocut-desktop is not named after its sdkwork-video-cut-pc root. The 11 migration-debt items (ten -pc-desktop aliases plus the inert manifest on sdkwork-im-harmony-mobile-host) do not contribute to this baseline because debt is non-fatal without --strict. Lower the baseline to 0 once those three packages are renamed.

DEPENDENCY_MANAGEMENT_SPEC.md section 1 ('Source/build dependency paths MUST be repository-relative, workspace-relative, or native package-manager coordinates ... MUST NOT be machine-specific absolute paths') and section 9 ('Source/build config contains no machine-specific absolute paths'). Both clauses had been normative since the spec was written and were executed by no gate, which is the structural reason the workspace accumulated absolute bindings: when it was moved off one drive they all broke at once and nothing failed up front. === RULES AUDITED BY DEFAULT === WORKSPACE-ABS: an absolute path whose segment chain contains the workspace basename, so it names the relocatable workspace root itself. SIBLING-REPO-ABS: an absolute path containing a sdkwork-<name> repository segment, which section 3 resolves through the consuming workspace mechanism instead. MACHINE-ABS: any other machine-rooted absolute path - a drive-rooted toolchain or installer-cache directory, a POSIX home directory, a Windows profile directory, or an MSYS drive mount. === SCOPE REVERSAL 2026-09-15 (this note's earlier revision said the opposite) === The previous revision put MACHINE-ABS behind an opt-in --include-machine-paths flag and justified it as 'a per-case decision'. That was wrong for the use this gate exists for: the request that drove this round was that no path may be hardcoded, because a pinned home directory, toolchain root, or installer cache is exactly what breaks on a different machine or a different operating system - the same failure the workspace-drive move produced, one machine away instead of one drive away. MACHINE-ABS is therefore in scope BY DEFAULT; --workspace-only is the narrow exit for 'did this touch reach the workspace root or a sibling checkout', and --include-machine-paths is retained as a no-op compatibility alias so nobody has to relearn a flag to keep the behaviour they just adopted. === CALIBRATION HISTORY: SEVEN FALSE-POSITIVE CLASSES AND TWO MECHANISM GAPS THIS GATE SHIPPED WITH === (1) The first draft matched the tail of URL schemes, so every https:// line in the fleet was reported; the drive branch is now guarded by a word-boundary lookbehind. (2) A file:/module URL reaches the scanner with its scheme gone, so every file:/// + absolute URL in the fleet was silently dropped; normalizeCandidate() collapses the leading slash run and drops the one slash the URL authority separator leaves in front of a drive letter. (3) A POSIX root of a single letter is not a filesystem root on any platform; measured, all 52 candidates that branch produced were HTTP routes, URI-normalisation examples or POSIX path test data, so the branch was removed rather than narrowed. (4) A regular-expression literal such as a two-character whitespace class normalises into a one-letter POSIX-looking path and landed on that same branch: 561 fleet findings, fixed by reading the RAW token before normalisation for a leading regex-escape prefix. (5) An escape in the SECOND and later alternative of an anchored pattern carries a backslash-escaped slash that no filesystem path literal contains, so a candidate containing one is now recognised as regex residue - the leading-token guard cannot see it, because the pattern opens with a word-boundary escape. (6) A three-digit octal escape is how a C or Java string literal spells a non-printable byte, and a generated protobuf descriptor offers the scanner an `e:` followed by octal escapes, which normalises into something drive-rooted; recognised and ignored. (7) An ellipsis segment is a documentation truncation, not a path component - no filesystem resolves a three-dot name as a child, so a path written with one is incomplete by construction and cannot be the working binding this gate exists to catch; three dots minimum, so a genuine two-dot component is still scanned. MECHANISM GAP A: an angle-bracket placeholder was cut at its closing bracket because the candidate body class excludes that character, so the truncated final segment failed the template test and the gate reported the very form section 1 tells authors to write - its only self-inflicted finding. Placeholders are now consumed as one unit. MECHANISM GAP B: `allow-fixture` is a prefix of `allow-fixture-block`, so a bare substring test read the block-scope marker as a file-scope declaration and reported two production Rust files that had marked their own cfg(test) module correctly; the file-scope marker is now matched with a boundary. SEPARATELY, the Program Files branch of the runtime-root exemption used to be unreachable, because the candidate scan ends a path at the first whitespace, so an install root arrived as a truncated prefix and was reported as a machine binding; the truncation is now recognised and ignored. === RESOLUTION: THE FIXTURE CLASS, NOW FOUR SCOPES === PORTABILITY_SPEC.md section 5.2 defines the exemption scopes, because what was originally recorded here as 'a per-file judgement call' needed a standard. (1) LINE SCOPE - `WORKSPACE-PATH:allow`, window 8 lines. A statement, not a physical line: rustfmt and prettier wrap one call across rows, so a correctly placed marker above a multi-line assertion was read as absent and 4 findings survived it - a gate defect, not author error. (2) FILE SCOPE - `WORKSPACE-PATH:allow-fixture` in the first 20 lines, honoured ONLY in a test file (basename *.test.* / *.spec.*, a tests|test|__tests__ path segment, or Rust's tests.rs / test_<subject>.rs). Genericizing a fixture is not an alternative: the sdkwork-<name> segment is frequently the value under assertion - a chunk name derived from the path, an application code derived from the directory, a derived surface directory, a simulated shell prompt - so renaming it deletes what the test asserts, while SIBLING-REPO-ABS cannot by itself tell a fixture from a real sibling reference. (3) DIRECTORY SCOPE - a marker FILE named `.workspace-path-fixture`, honoured only when the directory it sits in is itself test-scoped, for fixtures whose format has nowhere to put a comment (.json conformance corpora, .txt expected-output snapshots). (4) BLOCK SCOPE - `WORKSPACE-PATH:allow-fixture-block`, honoured only when written in a comment, exempting from the file's LAST real Rust cfg(test) declaration to end of file, for the unit-test modules that live inside production files and that no path-based test predicate can reach. The region is anchored to that declaration and NOT to the marker's own line: the committed gate started the block where the marker sat, so a marker on a production line exempted everything below it, including production code that ran to the test module. Anchoring to the last real declaration means the exemption can never begin above the trailing fixture region. Requiring the last rather than the first declaration matters in the other direction too: `paths.rs` carries an interior cfg(test) attribute at line 435 above its test module at 748. A marker's own position is otherwise free, because it is a declaration about the module and authors write it wherever the declaration reads best - 55 fleet files put it on the cfg(test) attribute and `paths.rs` puts it on the fixture expression inside the module. A first revision demanded the marker share the anchor's line; that rejected `paths.rs` and turned three ordinary PathBuf::from("C:/Users/<user>") test values into findings, so it was dropped. Outside a test file - or, for scopes 3 and 4, outside a test-scoped directory or off the cfg(test) line - a marker has no effect and is reported as FIXTURE-MARKER-NOT-APPLICABLE, and the scan CONTINUES past it, so no marker can suppress the findings it cannot legitimately exempt. Documentation files are excluded from that misuse check precisely so the rule can be written down. Both exemption counts and the list of exempt files are printed on every run, pass or fail, so no exemption is silent. === MEASURED 2026-09-15 === Progression of reported findings against the workspace checkout, every step re-measured rather than inferred: 3907 (starting point under the stricter scope, of which 561 were the regex-literal class) -> 3329 (regex guard plus MACHINE-ABS default-on) -> 3325 (the gate's own self-reference cleared) -> 984 (317 test-fixture file markers, candidate-boundary fix, 1 directory marker) -> 781 (60 Rust files marked on their cfg(test) line, tests.rs recognised) -> 729 (single-letter POSIX branch removed, 52 all-false positives) -> 724 (template segments, runtime-root trailing separator optional) -> 160 (98 files / 565 documentation placeholders) -> 124 (escaped-separator normalisation) -> 96 (atomic placeholders, octal escapes, the allow-fixture prefix boundary, the last workspace scripts) -> 60 (concrete paths in the workspace bin/ and bin/lib, video-cut / birdcoder2 / lockstep tooling, and 30 documentation and configuration sites) -> 15 (404 ellipsis-shaped prompt and snapshot literals) -> 0. Final run: 0 findings, 99861 files, 15 declared line exemptions, 402 fixture-exempt files, ~18s. Gate behaviour is pinned by tools/check-workspace-path-portability.test.mjs, raised from 12 to 26 tests: the file-scope, directory-scope and block-scope exemptions each have a positive case and a 'this marker does not exempt this' negative case, as do the angle-bracket, ellipsis, regex-alternative and octal-escape classes. SCOPE CAVEAT, RECORDED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: this baseline counts version-controlled source, configuration and documentation under the workspace root. The workspace ROOT governance layer itself - root package.json (the check:all contract), pnpm-workspace.yaml, configs/, tools/ and .sdkwork/ - is absent from this checkout, which is why the run-gate-matrix check:all cross-check fails with ENOENT on the workspace root package.json. That is a separate defect needing its own fix (re-materialise the root layer through the documented pack/deploy channel) and is deliberately not folded into this baseline. CROSS-SESSION NOTE: this portability round ran on a working tree shared with a sibling agent session; that session committed part of the fixes and rewrote the previous revision of this note during the same hour. Two edits to the gate were observed to be reverted mid-session by the concurrent writer and had to be re-applied, which is why the final state was re-measured from scratch instead of trusted from the diff.

REPOSITORY_BASELINE_SPEC.md section 2 ('A repository MUST NOT track compiler emit that sits beside its source') and section 5's forbidden-tracked clause, executed fleet-wide. These are the only two of audit-repository-baseline.mjs's twelve checks that describe repository CONTENT rather than L1 scaffolding, and they were structurally fail-open before this entry existed: both run only when named through --only, and all four runnable command lines the specs hand out pass --only branch-main (AGENTS.md, REPOSITORY_BASELINE_SPEC.md section 1, README.md, tools/sync-agent-main-branch-standard.mjs, which writes that narrowed line into every repository's AGENTS.md). The spec body asks for the whole audit and always did - section 5 'Run node tools/audit-repository-baseline.mjs --root <repo> before claiming repository baseline completion', section 6 'audit-repository-baseline.mjs passes for the repository root' - but no pipeline ran it, so 16 repositories accumulated 3017 tracked emit files (2026-09-23) with every gate green. WHY A WRAPPER RATHER THAN A MANIFEST ENTRY ON THE AUDIT ITSELF: this tier judges a gate by countItems(output) > baseline, and the audit prints only 'PASS <name> ([...])' / 'FAIL <name> ([...])' lines, none of which any of the four countItems readings recognise - registering the audit directly scores 0 items for a RED repository, which would have re-created the same fail-open one layer up. The wrapper reports 'violations : N' (N = failed checks, i.e. failing repository x failing check) and keeps the audit's own output contract untouched so the quoted command lines still parse. It is fail-closed in four directions: a non-directory workspace, a workspace with no sdkwork-* checkout, a --root that is not a git repository, and a child audit that returns fewer than two verdicts all exit 2 instead of reporting zero. MEASURED 2026-09-23: 100 repositories scanned, 0 violations, baseline 0. The two checks each had exactly one offender at the start of that round - sdkwork-notes (tracked-compiler-emit: sdkwork-notes-pc-react/scripts/shared-sdk-mode.d.ts, emitted from shared-sdk-mode.ts because tsconfig include reaches scripts/ and the fleet ignore block only covers src/ and composed/) and sdkwork-knowledgebase (forbidden-tracked: 14 files under sdks/sdkwork-knowledgebase-rpc-sdk/sdkwork-knowledgebase-rpc-sdk-typescript/dist/, the complete output of tsc -p tsconfig.json at outDir ./dist, a directory the root .gitignore already ignored because ignore never applies to tracked files) - both untracked, both working-tree copies preserved, both verified green afterwards. KNOWN SCOPE LIMITS, DELIBERATELY NOT WIDENED HERE because widening them changes REPOSITORY_BASELINE_SPEC.md section 2 and the gate together: (1) the tracked-compiler-emit extension family is *.js, *.js.map, *.d.ts and *.d.ts.map only, so a transpiled .mjs beside its .ts source and a double-suffixed foo.mjs.d.ts both escape - sdkwork-notes carries exactly that pair live; (2) the fleet ignore block's negation list (vite-env.d.ts, global.d.ts, shims.d.ts) is an enumeration and cannot be complete, since .gitignore cannot express 'ignore this only when a same-stem .ts sibling exists' - sdkwork-notes owns src/theme/sdkworkUiTheme.d.ts, a genuine declare module ambient that is absent from the list. A repository whose tsconfig include reaches outside src/ and composed/ must add its own ignore lines; the gate, not the ignore file, is the authority.
